benchmarks: LLM-generated multi-session persona dialogues (Park et al. 2023 dataset, avg 11.9 sessions/dialogue)
fallos_mitigaciones: Growing memory pool of persona facts/knowledge triples over many sessions raises computational/latency concerns, and fine-grained forgetting of outdated traits or events is explicitly flagged as unresolved; no mitigation implemented (Limitations section).
cita: Chen et al. (2025). Post Persona Alignment for Multi-Session Dialogue Generation.
notes: §3.1 history compressed to (name,relation,object) persona-fact triples via LLM extraction, verbalized and stored in a memory module (SEMANTICA). §3.2 PPA reverses retrieval order: generate general response Rg first, then use Rg as the query (SentenceBERT cosine similarity, top-k=5, threshold 0.2) to retrieve persona memories, then refine. Table1: PPA C-Score 0.456 / Entropy 5.75 / P-F1 0.146 vs best baseline SimOAP 0.206/5.07/0.100. Table2 (query-type ablation, mide_lectura evidence): Context-query 0.363 -> Response(Rg)-query 0.456 -> Gold-query 0.554 C-Score, confirming response-guided retrieval hypothesis. benchmarks: PerLTQA (own dataset, 8,593 QA pairs / 30-141 characters); retrieval models compared: BM25, DPR, Contriever
cita: Du et al. (2024). PerLTQA: A Personal Long-Term Memory Dataset for Memory Classification, Retrieval, and Synthesis in Question Answering.
notes: §3 dataset construction (6-step LLM-generated per character): profiles+social-relationships=semantic memory, events+dialogues=episodic memory, 8,593 evaluation QA pairs for 30 characters. Static pre-built memory bank -- no runtime write/consolidation/forgetting mechanism evaluated -> operaciones=NA, trigger=NA. §4.2-4.4 pipeline: memory classification (BERT best, P95.96/R95.64/F1 95.74) -> memory retrieval (Table5: BM25 R@1=0.705 in 0.03s vs DPR R@1=0.602 in 2.96s, DPR overtakes BM25 by k=3) -> memory synthesis (Table3: MAP 0.756/Corr.0.573 with classification+retrieval vs MAP 0.156/Corr.0.088 without retrieval -- retrieval dominates, classification alone contributes little). §5.1 Table6 ablation (NR/IR/CR: no/incorrect/correct retrieval) shows correct retrieval sharply raises MAP/Correctness across 5 LLMs.

benchmarks: LoCoMo (modified: 12 longest dialogues + padding session + added per-response timestamps); custom Time-based / Ambiguous Time-based / Time+Content query dataset (TemporalMemoryDataset)
fallos_mitigaciones: Pure semantic/embedding retrieval completely fails on time- and meta-data-based conversational queries (recall<10 at k=10-30, Table1) and on ambiguous pronoun/demonstrative queries (Table2, recall 2.9); mitigated via a hybrid tabular chain-of-table (deterministic f_value/f_between meta-data query functions) + semantic-vector retrieval pipeline, gated by an LLM query-type classifier and an LLM query-rewrite disambiguation step (Table1: recall jumps to ~90-94 with CoTable+Semantic; Table2: Query-Rewrite recall 89.4 vs Original-Query recall 2.9).
cita: Alonso et al. (2024). Toward Conversational Agents with Context and Time Sensitive Long-term Memory.
notes: §3 dataset: modified LoCoMo + 3 new query types testing conversational meta-data (time/session) retrieval and ambiguity, distinct from pure content-based retrieval. §4 model: tabular chat DB (meta-data columns + vector-DB content column, HIBRIDA) + LLM query-type classifier + chain-of-table meta-data search (GREP-ARCHIVOS-like exact-match f_value/f_between) + semantic vector retrieval (EMBEDDINGS) + LLM query-rewrite for disambiguation. §5 Table1: plain Semantic retrieval fails time-based queries (recall 2-6/F2 2-6); CoTable+Semantic reaches recall ~90-94/F2 ~78-88 (hMistral7b/GPT3.5). Table2: query-rewrite ablation on ambiguous queries.

benchmarks: TextWorld (Treasure Hunt, Cleaning, Cooking, 3 difficulty levels each); NetHack (via NetPlay); Musique; HotpotQA (200 samples each)
fallos_mitigaciones: Stale/outdated semantic facts (e.g., object/player location changes) mislead the agent if not removed; AriGraph explicitly detects outdated edges by comparing newly extracted triplets against existing ones incident to the same vertices and removes them before expanding memory (section 'Constructing AriGraph'); Cleaning-game analysis (section 5.1) attributes Ariadne's gain specifically to filtering outdated location info vs history-accumulating baselines (Full-history, Episodic-only) that underperform there.
cita: Anokhin et al. (2024). AriGraph: Learning Knowledge Graph World Models with Episodic Memory for LLM Agents.
notes: Memory graph G=(Vs,Es,Ve,Ee): semantic triplets (obj1,rel,obj2) extracted per observation + episodic vertices/edges (WRITE); outdated-edge detection+removal on every write (OLVIDO+ACTUALIZACION) -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Retrieval: Contriever/BGE-M3 semantic search (depth/width d,w) over graph structure (GRAFO) then episodic-vertex relevance scoring formula Eq.1 (RANKING). Ariadne agent: working memory holds goal+plan+recent history+retrieved knowledge; planning module creates/updates a sub-goal plan stored back to working memory -> plan_estado=SI. Section 5.1 Fig.3: same planner/decision-maker, memory-module swapped across Full-history/Summarization/RAG/RAG+Reflexion/Simulacra/AriGraph (component ABLATION) on Treasure-Hunt/Cleaning/Cooking TextWorld games, AriGraph wins all three; also beats RL baselines GATA/LTL-GATA/EXPLORER (Fig.4). Section 5.2 NetHack Table1: Ariadne[Room obs] 593+-203 score/6.33 levels vs NetPlay[Room obs] 342+-109/3.67 vs oracle NetPlay[Level obs] 675+-130/7.33. Section 5.3 Table2: Musique/HotpotQA multi-hop QA vs GraphRAG/HOLMES/ReadAgent/GraphReader, >10x cheaper than GraphRAG (COSTO-TOKENS, Table3 Appx D).

fallos_mitigaciones: The loop's self-attribution (decision observability) is reliable for detecting fixes but blind to detecting regressions from an edit (Fig.4: fix precision/recall far above a random-prediction baseline, but regression precision/recall near/below it); left unmitigated, flagged as the clearest direction for future self-evolution loops. Separately, harness components interact non-additively: the three positive single-component gains (memory/tools/middleware) sum to +11.1pp vs full AHE's measured +7.3pp aggregate gain, because memory+middleware+prompt push toward the same closure-style re-verification and waste turns on redundant re-checks (section 4.4.1, Table 3).
cita: Lin et al. (2026). Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses.
notes: RECONSIDERAR: this paper's primary focus is offline harness/prompt-engineering automation (an Evolve Agent iteratively edits system-prompt/tools/middleware/long-term-memory as static files of a coding-agent harness across benchmark iterations, section 3), not an agent's own runtime memory-management during a single task; 'long-term memory' is only one of four ablated harness components, and F_screening arrived blank in the input (populated here from full-text read). Section 3.1: memory is a FILE-based harness component (DOCS-ARCHIVOS) written/edited by the offline Evolve Agent based on LLM-discretionary evidence-driven decisions (trigger=DISCRECIONAL-LLM), reverted at file granularity if a next-round verdict rejects it (WRITE/ACTUALIZACION/OLVIDO, Algorithm 1 ROLLBACK step); no runtime retrieval/ranking mechanism is described for how the Code Agent accesses memory content within one task (presumably always fully loaded, like the system prompt) -> retrieval=NA. Table 3 (section 4.4.1): swapping AHE's long-term-memory component alone into the NexAU0 seed raises Terminal-Bench2 pass@1 69.7%->75.3% (Hard tier 51.7%->63.3%, exceeding even full AHE's 53.3% there) -- memory holds '12 boundary-case lessons' (procedural insights on performance margin, queued-over-limit cancellation, evaluator-style closure, source-packaging layout) -> mem_tipos=PROCEDIMENTAL, mide_lectura=SI. Section 3.3/Fig.4: every edit ships a self-declared prediction later verified against next-round observed task deltas -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI.
